ui.descricao.MG: Running, kicking, throwing, jumping and whole-body coordination.

ui.descricao.ES: Climbing up and down safely on steps, climbing frames and walls.
ui.descricao.LA: Hand/foot preference, midline, sense of right and left.
ui.avanco.nenhum: No area improved between the first and the last assessment of the period.
ui.avanco.geralIgual: The overall score stayed the same.

ui.relatorio.subtitulo: Choose the assessments, review the text of the most recent one and generate the PDF for the parents.
ui.relatorio.barrasDica: The bar chart only shows the 4 most recent of the selection; the progress line uses all of them.
ui.relatorio.textoDica: Changes are saved to the assessment. Notes per area are edited in the assessment itself.

ui.relatorio.erro: Could not generate the PDF. Try again; if it keeps failing, reload the app.
ui.pdf.comoLerLead: During the assessment, the therapist observes the child in everyday and play activities, organised into seven areas of movement.
ui.pdf.respostasTitulo: Each activity gets one of three answers
ui.pdf.resposta.2: the child does the activity alone and safely (2 points).
ui.pdf.resposta.1: the child tries, does part of it or needs help (1 point).
ui.pdf.resposta.0: the child cannot do it yet (0 points).
ui.pdf.percentual1: In each area, we add up the points and compare them with the maximum possible. 100% means the child does every activity in that area; 50% means they are halfway there. The overall score is the average of the seven areas.
ui.pdf.percentual2: The activities change with age (bands of 0 to 2, 2 to 4, 4 to 6, 6 to 9 and 9 to 15 years). That is why we use percentages: it lets us compare assessments even when the child moves to another band.
ui.pdf.importanteTexto: This is an internal clinical follow-up tool, not a standardised and validated scale. Age milestones are references and are not a diagnosis. Talk to the therapist about any questions.
ui.pdf.evolucaoDica: Each coloured line is an area; the thicker black line is the overall score. The dashed line marks when the age band changed.
ui.pdf.evolucaoVazia: The progress line appears from the second assessment on. This report includes one assessment, from {data}.
ui.pdf.comparativo1: Percentage by area in the assessment of {data}.
ui.pdf.comparativoN: The {n} most recent assessments, from oldest (light shade) to most recent (strong shade).
ui.pdf.itemLead: Answers from the most recent assessment ({data}, band {faixa}: {rotulo}).
ui.pdf.itemLeadAnteriores: Answers from the most recent assessment ({data}, band {faixa}: {rotulo}), next to earlier ones when the activity is the same.
ui.pdf.traco: — means the activity was not part of that assessment (another age band).

MF: Offer play dough, clay or bread dough to squeeze, roll and shape.
Play at picking up small objects with the fingers (beans, buttons, clothes pegs), always supervised.
Draw, paint and cut out together, starting with large paper and chunky crayons.
Encourage the child to dress on their own: buttoning, zipping, putting on shoes.
MG: Play outdoors every day: running, jumping, kicking and throwing a ball.
Set up small obstacle courses at home with cushions, chairs and ropes.
Ride a bike, scooter or tricycle, depending on age.
EE: Play "musical statues", freezing when the music stops.
Challenge them to stand on one foot while counting to five, switching feet.
Games imitating animals standing still (flamingo, stork).
ED: Walk along a tape line on the floor, forwards and backwards.
Play hopscotch and hop on one foot.
Walk along a low kerb or a log in the park, holding hands at first.
Play "Simon says" with changes of direction and stops.
EN: Play at crawling around the house like animals (cat, bear).
Build tunnels with chairs and a sheet to crawl under.
All-fours races on the rug or on the grass.
ES: Go to playgrounds with ladders, slides and climbing frames, supervised.
Go up and down stairs calmly, alternating feet.
Climb piled-up cushions or the sofa, teaching how to get down safely.
LA: Games with right and left commands ("right hand on your head").
Crossed clapping games and mirror games.
Ask them to pick up objects placed on the opposite side of the body.
Use the way to school to name turning right and left.
